answer: In an agent marketplace, atlas, beacon and willow must each lock the same deposit for 30 days before gaining one vote on how shared funds are spent. The protocol counts only identities backed by separate, simultaneously locked deposits, so the same coins cannot support multiple votes. An attacker seeking 1,000 fake voters must immobilize 1,000 deposits for a month, tying influence to capital and imposing a financing cost even if every deposit is later returned.
